meta.scope: Mexico batch 5 — monthly industrial/commercial/services surveys, construction, poverty lines & multidimensional poverty framework, tourism satellite account, unpaid household work satellite account. Continues expansion toward 150+ candidates.

candidates.title: Encuesta Mensual de la Industria Manufacturera (EMIM) / Monthly Survey of the Manufacturing Industry
candidates.description: Monthly establishment survey of manufacturing activity. Produces indicators of production, employed personnel, hours worked and real average remuneration. Core high-frequency input into the Indicador Mensual de la Actividad Industrial (IMAI) and national accounts.
candidates.notes: Primary monthly manufacturing survey. Explicitly listed among the main sources of the IMAI (together with ENEC, mining statistics and ENOE). Regular bulletins publish month-on-month and year-on-year changes in production, employment, hours and wages.

candidates.title: Encuesta Mensual sobre Empresas Comerciales (EMEC) / Monthly Survey of Commercial Enterprises
candidates.description: Monthly survey of wholesale and retail commercial enterprises. Tracks real income from supply of goods and services, employed personnel, remunerations and related variables at national and state level. Operating continuously since the 1980s (originally Mexico City metro area, later national).
candidates.notes: Key high-frequency commerce indicator. Sample covers thousands of commercial enterprises; results published monthly with seasonally adjusted series for wholesale and retail. Direct input into short-term economic monitoring and national-accounts compilation.

candidates.title: Encuesta Mensual de Servicios (EMS) / Monthly Survey of Services
candidates.description: Monthly survey of private non-financial services (including transport, storage and related activities). Produces indicators of real income, employment, expenses and remunerations at national and state level.
candidates.notes: Completes the trio of high-frequency establishment surveys (manufacturing, commerce, services) that feed short-term activity indicators and the national accounts.

candidates.title: Encuesta Nacional de Empresas Constructoras (ENEC) / National Survey of Construction Companies
candidates.description: Monthly survey of construction enterprises. Measures the evolution of construction activity and is one of the principal statistical sources used in the compilation of the Indicador Mensual de la Actividad Industrial (IMAI) for the construction sector.
candidates.notes: Documented source for the construction component of IMAI. Methodology notes for IMAI list ENEC together with EMIM, mining statistics and ENOE as main inputs.

candidates.title: Líneas de Pobreza por Ingresos (LPI / LPEI) / Income Poverty Lines
candidates.description: Monetary poverty lines (urban and rural) representing the monthly cost of the food basket (extreme poverty line) and the food + non-food basic basket (poverty line). Updated monthly using the INPC. Used as the income threshold in Mexico’s multidimensional poverty measurement.
candidates.notes: High-frequency social indicator. Values are updated with the INPC; July 2026 urban LPI was reported around 4 884 pesos per person per month. Forms the economic-wellbeing dimension of the official multidimensional poverty measure. After institutional changes, INEGI has taken a larger direct role in the poverty measurement and line updates.

candidates.title: Medición Multidimensional de la Pobreza / Multidimensional Poverty Measurement
candidates.publisher: INEGI (methodology originally developed under CONEVAL / Ley General de Desarrollo Social)
candidates.description: Official multidimensional poverty measure. A person is in poverty when income is below the poverty line and at least one of six social-rights deprivations is present (education, health services, social security, housing quality/spaces, basic housing services, food). Extreme poverty combines income below the extreme line with more severe deprivation. Results published periodically (often aligned with ENIGH cycles).
candidates.notes: Central social-policy indicator. Relies on ENIGH (and related modules) for income and deprivation data and on the income poverty lines. Recent figures (around 2024 measurement) indicate substantial reductions in both income poverty and multidimensional poverty relative to 2018. The underlying methodology document remains a key static reference that is cited every measurement cycle.

candidates.title: Cuenta Satélite del Turismo de México (CSTM) / Satellite Account of Tourism of Mexico
candidates.description: Satellite account measuring the economic contribution of tourism within the SCNM framework. Reports tourism GDP, employment in tourism activities, and detailed breakdowns by characteristic tourism products and activities. Base year currently 2018.
candidates.notes: 2024 results: tourism GDP ≈ 2.71 trillion pesos (8.7% of total economy); ≈ 2.9 million paid jobs (7.4% of national total). Constructed from the Supply and Use Tables, Input-Output Matrix and Goods-and-Services accounts of the SCNM.

candidates.title: Cuenta Satélite del Trabajo No Remunerado de los Hogares de México (CSTNRHM) / Satellite Account of Unpaid Household Work
candidates.description: Satellite account that assigns an economic value to unpaid domestic and care work performed by household members. Complements the conventional GDP by making visible a large volume of work that falls outside market production boundaries.
candidates.notes: 2024 results: economic value of unpaid domestic and care work ≈ 8 trillion pesos — larger than manufacturing or commerce as a share of conventional GDP. Women account for the majority of the hours and value. Provides the macroeconomic counterpart to time-use and care-economy analysis and links to the health satellite account’s unpaid-work component.

proposed_edges.basis: IMAI methodology explicitly lists EMIM as a principal source for manufacturing activity.
IMAI methodology lists ENEC as a principal source for construction activity.
Poverty lines are updated monthly with the INPC using the prices of the goods and services in the urban and rural baskets.
Income dimension of multidimensional poverty is defined relative to the income poverty lines.
ENIGH (and related modules) supplies the household income and social-deprivation data used in the multidimensional measure.
Tourism satellite account is built from the SCNM Supply-and-Use Tables, Input-Output Matrix and Goods-and-Services accounts.
Unpaid-work satellite account is constructed as a satellite to the national accounts framework.
